summary.headline: Camlin Q1 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to INR5,199 million, but EBITDA margin collapsed to about 4% from 45% last quarter on raw material costs and vanillin under-utilisation.
summary.overview: Revenue reached INR5,199 million, up about 28% YoY and about INR1,000 million QoQ, but margins fell sharply on raw material, freight and logistics costs tied to the West Asia conflict. The company reorganised reporting into Specialty Ingredients, Aroma and Performance Chemicals, with Aroma and Performance Chemicals both EBITDA-negative or near zero in the quarter. Ethyl vanillin ramp-up ran at low utilisation, and FY27 vanillin volume guidance was cut to about 3,000 tons from 3,600-4,000 tons. Management cut FY27 EBITDA margin guidance to 10-12% while keeping revenue guidance, and debt was flat at about INR640 crore gross.

segments.name: Specialty Ingredients (blends and straights)
segments.commentary: Revenue above INR4,000 million with blends above INR3,000 million; EBITDA margin 6.35%. Management says about 4-5% of gross margin was lost to raw material costs and Brazil air-freight, with Brazil's shortfall of about INR8 crore expected to correct in Q2.

segments.name: Aroma (vanillin)
segments.commentary: Sold about 560 tons (350 t ethyl, 200 t methyl from channel stock) against 6,000-ton capacity; produced ~400 tons. Quarterly EBITDA negative at INR4-4.5 crore on fixed cost absorption; management expects positive EBITDA in Q2.

segments.name: Performance Chemicals
segments.commentary: Gross segment revenue about INR175 crore, of which ~INR130 crore is internal transfer, leaving ~INR40 crore external sales. EBITDA margin 2.5% with diphenol plant shut; management expects positive EBITDA from Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance: INR2,200-2,300 crore, versus earlier INR2,000-2,400 crore; management says top line is secure.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance cut to 10-12% (10-11% per CFO/MD), implying about INR220-230 crore EBITDA, versus earlier INR250-280 crore.
Analyst read-back: average run rate of about INR70 crore EBITDA per quarter for remaining quarters; management did not dispute this.
Q3 FY27 expected to return to double-digit consolidated EBITDA margin; H2 margin of 13-15% floated by an analyst, not disputed.
FY28 EBITDA margin in the range of 12-14%.
Vanillin FY27 volume about 3,000 tons (earlier 3,600-4,000); 4 campaigns planned, Q2 volume 500-600 tons, Q3 1,000+ tons. Capacity 6,000 tons, achievable 5,000 tons with 3 campaigns.
Blends growth of at least 20% in FY27; budget assumes 25-30%.
capex_capacity: Vanillin capacity 6,000 tons per year; ethyl vanillin campaign of about 750 tons ran through mid-August, with about 350 tons sold and over 300 tons produced; methyl vanillin campaign to follow after roughly two weeks of changeover.
Diphenol plant shut because phenol and raw material prices are high; hydroquinone secured from China for the next two quarters; decision on alternate use or restart by Q3 FY27.
Working capital cycle about 100 days on a consolidated basis; each INR1 crore of revenue growth needs about one-third as working capital support.
CFS Europe in liquidation with no further cash burn beyond legal costs; China subsidiary liquidation expected to cost INR10-20 million in Q1.
demand_pricing: Channel stocks in the US and China described as cleared; management sees demand picking up and is negotiating quarterly, half-yearly and annual contracts with F&F customers.
US and Europe ethyl vanillin realisations stated at about $13-14/kg; methyl vanillin raw material cost $7-8/kg, with conversion cost about INR7 crore/month fixed.
Management sees a supply gap of about 5,000-6,000 tons in US and Europe that must be imported; Syensqo (Solvay) is the market leader; Chinese imports priced around $15 against Solvay's $18.
Pass-through of raw material increases to blends customers is lagging by one quarter; management expects to recover about half of the cost increase in Q2.
Trade financing (dealer finance) on purchase and sales sides costs an estimated 1-1.5% and is hitting gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 EBITDA guidance achievable given Q1 EBITDA of about INR9 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management restated guidance as INR2,200-2,300 crore revenue with 10-11% margin, which it said is within reach on the current cost structure; it expects about 10% margin over the next nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Aroma EBITDA negative and what is its normalised economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said low utilisation (about 400 tons produced vs 1,500-ton quarterly capacity) left fixed cost unabsorbed. Management said 70-80% utilisation would make the business profitable and gave about 7% EBITDA at $13/kg on 3,000 tons.

qa_highlights.question: How much debt reduction and what external funding is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt is INR640 crore, down from INR670 crore on 31 March. The CFO said INR100-200 crore of working capital lines are expected within 1-1.5 months, and equity or other capital is being considered without a decision yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 vanillin volume cut from 3,600-4,000 tons to about 3,000?
qa_highlights.answer: The ethyl vanillin ramp-up was slower to secure quality, with 95% customer approval. Each campaign switch costs about a month, and four campaigns are planned this year.

qa_highlights.question: What would Q1 EBITDA have been under normal conditions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 4-5% of gross margin was lost, which would have lifted EBITDA to roughly INR37-40 crore, an analyst's figure that management confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Will raw material cost pressure persist into Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects elevated raw material prices to persist through Q2 and guidance assumes about three months of elevated costs, not six or nine months.

risks_watch: Q2 FY27 delivery against the claim that Aroma turns EBITDA-positive and Performance Chemicals turns positive once diphenol is idle; Q1 Aroma EBITDA was negative INR4-4.5 crore.
Raw material pass-through: management expects to recover only about half of the cost increase in blends in Q2, and elevated input prices are assumed for three months, not six or nine.

Liquidity and funding: gross debt INR640 crore, working capital needs rising with the longer cycle (about 100 days), and INR100-200 crore of credit lines plus possible equity or other capital still undecided.
Vanillin volume: FY27 cut to about 3,000 tons; Q2 500-600 tons; Q3 1,000+ tons needed to deliver the H2 margin recovery. Each campaign switch costs about a month.
Diphenol plant shut with a decision on alternate use or restart due by Q3 FY27; hydroquinone sourced from China for two quarters.
Trade financing (dealer finance) costs of about 1-1.5% now hitting gross margin; the Brazil air-freight hit of about INR8 crore is expected to reverse in Q2.
key_quotes: Obviously, we have done extremely well on the revenues, but the margins are not in line with the expectations, but there were certain reasons for that.
The whole issue is on the margins.
So, on sales side, it's not a problem at all. The whole issue is on the purchase side.
Looking at the scenario, I think we will be able to just revisit these margins, and we feel that now the margin should be in the range of 10% to 12% this year.
Now, when the methyl vanillin starts, you will see that the margins will be significantly better, the gross margin.
The third is, of course, capital, which we are looking at different various options to be able to raise that capital.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on top-line delivery and on a margin recovery from Q2-Q3, but cautious on raw material costs, the Aroma ramp-up and funding. Several answers were hedged, with capital raising described as undecided, and the margin guidance was cut twice in the call's framing.

adds.what: Vanillin capacity 6,000 t/yr already in place (no new addition); diphenol plant shut with restart or alternate-use decision by Q3 FY27

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR2,200-2,300 crore (midpoint ~INR2,250 crore), and vanillin volume was cut to ~3,000 t with utilisation near 25%, while no new capacity is being added and the diphenol plant is shut, so growth is not clearly backed by capacity.
